title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO: what we know
excerpt: Nvidia's board brought Jensen Huang back as CEO on 23 November, 11 days after he resigned. Here is what is confirmed, what is not, and what to watch.
body:
> **Quick answer.** On Monday 23 November 2026 Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. The investigation into the foreign intelligence reports continues.

## What happened

On Monday, 23 November 2026, Nvidia [announced](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045810/000104581026000090/nov23pressrelease.htm) that Jensen Huang is president, chief executive and a board member again, effective immediately. The board voted unanimously. Huang resigned on 12 November, so he was out for 11 days.

Colette Kress, who was interim CEO, keeps her role as chief financial officer. Harvey C. Jones stays on as board chair.

## Why Huang left, and what the board says now

Huang resigned after disclosing "personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct," Jones said on 17 November, according to NPR. News reports tied him to a woman US intelligence officials say was recruited by China's spy agency, and to a second woman who is a Nvidia executive. NPR said it had not independently confirmed those reports. Her former employer, Megaspeed, told NPR it conducts legitimate and lawful business.

Nvidia's statement says the board held "a series of discussions and meetings" with Huang and was "satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead." It also says the board took input from "senior levels of the United States government" and is confident, based on that input, that his return "poses no national security risk."

This is a sharp turn. On the company's earnings call on 17 November, Jones had said the board did not intend to reinstate Huang, [NPR reported](https://www.nhpr.org/2026-11-17/nvidia-board-says-it-does-not-intend-to-reinstate-jensen-huang-as-ceo). [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/23/nvidia-reverses-course-and-brings-jensen-huang-back-as-ceo/) says Nvidia had even hired an executive search firm, and that a group of tech executives, including Elon Musk, had signed a petition asking for his return.

President Trump [endorsed the move](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/23/trump-endorses-jensen-huangs-return-to-nvidia-says-us-has-no-evidence-of-wrongdoing/) on Truth Social. He said the Attorney General had confirmed the government has no evidence Huang broke the law. TechCrunch notes the Attorney General has not yet made a formal statement, and calls it an unusual claim for a president to make, since the Attorney General normally investigates independently. Trump also said Nvidia should continue its internal export-control investigation.

## What is confirmed and what is not

Confirmed by Nvidia: the reinstatement, the unanimous vote, and that the independent-director committee investigating reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort will "proceed to conclusion." Nvidia says Huang supports it and is committed to cooperating.

The board also set up a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors, and has started a search for a new Chief Compliance Officer. Nvidia says it will keep cooperating with government investigations.

Not settled: the investigation's findings. NPR reported last week that Huang and Nvidia's general counsel are due to answer questions behind closed doors from House committees on 1 and 2 December, about alleged chip smuggling and export-control evasion.

![Two bars: Nvidia shares down more than 16% since early November, then up 27% on reinstatement day](/assets/blog/nvidia-reinstates-jensen-huang-ceo-art-share-move-hd.jpg "Nvidia shares: down more than 16% since early November (NPR, 17 Nov), then up 27% by 9:51 am ET on 23 Nov (TechCrunch).")

## What the market did

TechCrunch reported Nvidia shares opened about 30% higher on Monday, and were up 27%, at $159.95, by 9:51 am ET. NPR reported on 17 November that the stock had dropped more than 16% since early November, after Huang disclosed the affair.

## What to watch

The committee's findings, the December hearings, and who fills the compliance role. The export-control questions have not gone away.

## My take

The board changed course within a week, with the government's input cited as a reason. I'd treat the company's confidence as a statement, not a finding, and wait for the investigation before drawing conclusions.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Jensen Huang CEO of Nvidia again?

Yes. Nvidia announced on 23 November 2026 that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president and CEO and as a board member, effective immediately. He had resigned on 12 November. Colette Kress, who was interim CEO, keeps her CFO role.

### Why did Nvidia's board bring Huang back?

The board says it held a series of discussions with Huang, was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead, and received input from senior levels of the US government and is confident, based on that input, that his return poses no national security risk. Days earlier, board chair Harvey Jones had said it did not intend to reinstate him.

### Is the investigation into Nvidia over?

No. Nvidia says the independent committee investigating reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will proceed to conclusion, and that Huang is committed to cooperating. The board also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee and has started a search for a Chief Compliance Officer.

### What happened to Nvidia's stock?

TechCrunch reported shares opened about 30% higher on 23 November and were up 27%, at $159.95, by 9:51 am ET. NPR had reported on 17 November that the stock had fallen more than 16% since early November.
